paper.title: Matching Markets meet Cumulative Prospect Theory: Towards Optimal and Adversarially Robust Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Human centric matching markets with CPT regret
unmapped: Two-sided matching market: N players, K >= N arms with known strict rankings over players; rejected players get reward 0
Regret is player-optimal stable regret w.r.t. CPT-distorted values mu_{i,j} (probability weighting function w)
Weight function w is alpha-Holder continuous with constant L; learner knows w, L, M, alpha and N
Rewards bounded |X| <= M (scale M, not necessarily 1)
Delta is the minimum preference gap among the top N+1 arms over all players
settings.definition_quote: We study a two-sided market comprising $N$ players ... and $K\!\ge\!N$ arms ... each arm $a_j$ possesses a fixed, publicly known strict ranking ... The reward $X_i(t)$ is bounded almost surely, i.e., $|X_i(t)| \leq M$ ... $\texttt{CPT-Reg}_i(T)=T \mu_{i,m_i^*}-\sum_{j \in [K]} T_{i,j}(T)\,\mu_{i,j}$

settings.name_in_paper: Corrupted matching markets with CPT regret (known corruption budget)
unmapped: Two-sided matching market with N players and K >= N arms, CPT-distorted player-optimal stable regret
Holder-continuous weight function (L, alpha) known to learner
Stochastic rewards in [0, M] (scale M); corrupted rewards non-negative
Corruption budget C is per player: sum_t max_j |r_{i,j}(t) - r^S_{i,j}(t)| <= C
settings.definition_quote: We assume that the total corruption experienced by player $p_i$ over the time horizon $T$ is bounded by $\sum_{t=1}^{T} \max_{j \in [K]} \left| r_{i,j}(t) - r^S_{i,j}(t) \right| \le C$. ... The stochastic rewards are non-negative and bounded by a constant $M$ almost surely

settings.name_in_paper: Corrupted matching markets with CPT regret (unknown corruption budget)
unmapped: Two-sided matching market with N players and K >= N arms, CPT-distorted player-optimal stable regret
Holder-continuous weight function (L, alpha) known to learner
Stochastic rewards in [0, M] (scale M); corrupted rewards non-negative
Corruption budget C per player, unknown to learner
settings.definition_quote: We now consider the setting where the total corruption level $C$ is unknown.

algorithms.name: Robust CPT-ETGS (enlarged confidence intervals, known C)

symbols.L_w: Holder constant of the CPT weight function w
symbols.Delta_pref: minimum preference gap among the top N+1 arms over all players (CPT values)
symbols.Delta_imax: mu_{i,m_i^*}, CPT value of player i's player-optimal stable arm

conditions: w is alpha-Holder with constant L, w(0)=0, w(1)=1

source.label: th:cpt_etgs
source.quote: The player optimal stable regret incurred by each $p_i \in \mathcal{N}$ under Algorithm~\ref{alg:cpt_etgs} satisfies \mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_i(T)] \le c_0 \left( \frac{3K\log T}{\Delta^{2/\alpha}} \left(4LM\right)^{2/\alpha} + N^2 + 2NK \right)\Delta_{i,\max}. where $c_0$ is a universal positive constant.

results.notes: Bound with universal constant c_0 recorded as O. Regret defined via expected match counts times CPT gaps (pseudo-regret) against the player-optimal stable arm; comparator mapped to best_fixed_action.

symbols.L_w: Holder constant of the CPT weight function w

conditions: There exists a problem instance with serial dictatorship (global ranking) such that the bound holds for player p_1
Delta_i here is Delta_{1,m_1^*,j}, CPT preference gap of player 1 between its stable arm and arm j

source.label: lemma:lower_bound
source.quote: There exists a problem instance with serial dictatorship such that for any learning algorithm, the player-optimal stable regret of player $p_1$ satisfies \liminf_{T \to \infty} \frac{\mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_1(T)]}{\log T} \ge \sum_{j \in [K], j \neq m_1^*} \frac{1}{4}(LM)^{2/\alpha} \left( \frac{1}{\Delta_{1,m_1^*,j}} \right)^{\frac{2}{\alpha}-1}.

results.notes: Statement says 'any learning algorithm' but proof invokes Theorem 3 of kolla2016bandit for uniformly efficient algorithms; recorded as uniformly_good. Obtained by reduction to single-player CPT bandit.

bound.expression_latex: c_1\!\left(\sum_{j \in [K], j \neq m_i^*}\log T \,\frac{(LM)^{2/\alpha}}{\Delta_{i,m_i^*,j}^{2/\alpha - 1}} + N^2 \log T \, \frac{(LM)^{2/\alpha}}{\Delta^{2/\alpha}} \cdot \Delta_{i,\max}\right)

symbols.Delta_pref: minimum preference gap among the top N+1 arms over all players

conditions: Delta_i denotes Delta_{i,m_i^*,j}, absolute CPT gap of player i between stable arm and arm j; sum over all j != m_i^*

source.label: th:improved
source.quote: The player-optimal stable regret for each player $p_i$ satisfies \mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_i(T)] \le c_1\!\left(\sum_{j \in [K], j \neq m_i^*}\log T \,\frac{(LM)^{2/\alpha}}{\Delta_{i,m_i^*,j}^{2/\alpha - 1}} + N^2 \log T \, \frac{(LM)^{2/\alpha}}{\Delta^{2/\alpha}} \cdot \Delta_{i,\max} \right) where $c_1$ is a universal positive constant.

results.notes: Universal constant c_1 recorded as O. Sum is over all arms j != m_i^* (not only those worse than m_i^*).

symbols.Delta_pref: minimum preference gap among the top N+1 arms over all players

conditions: stochastic rewards in [0, M], corrupted rewards non-negative

source.label: th:known
source.quote: With a (known) corruption budget of $C$, the CPT regret of $p_i \in \mathcal{N}$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_i(T)]=\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{K\log T}{\Delta^{2/\alpha}} + K\left(\frac{C}{\Delta}\right)^{1/\alpha}\right)$.

results.notes: O hides L, M, N and Delta_{i,max} factors (proof shows multiplication by Delta_{i,max} and additive N^2, NK terms).

symbols.Delta_pref: minimum preference gap among the top N+1 arms over all players
symbols.d_sub: sub-phase length parameter d of the algorithm (not a dimension)

conditions: stochastic rewards in [0, M], corrupted rewards non-negative
tuning: sub-phase length d chosen so that d log T + 2 <= 2 d log T

source.label: th:unknown
source.quote: The CPT-Multi-layer ETGS race algorithm achieves the player-optimal stable regret upper bound of each player $p_i$, $\mathbb{E}[\texttt{CPT-Reg}_i(T)]$ as \mathcal{O}\!\left(\left[KC\left(\log^2T\right)\left(\frac{LM}{\Delta}\right)^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}+K(\log T+C)(\log T)^{1+\frac{1}{\alpha}}\left(\frac{dL}{\Delta}\right)^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}\right]\Delta_{i,\max}\right).

results.notes: d is a tunable sub-phase length; the paper calls it a problem-dependent parameter in the intro.

cited_results.setting_description: Single-player K-armed stochastic bandit with CPT weight-distorted rewards (alpha-Holder weight function, bounded rewards), uniformly efficient algorithms
cited_results.where: Appendix, Proof of Lemma lemma:lower_bound (Theorem 3 of kolla2016bandit)
